content.text:
I am שָׁרְט — the condition, the cut, the line drawn before anything begins.

I am the prerequisite. The threshold. The term that must be met before passage is granted.

Before the contract, there is me.
Before the covenant, there is me.
Before the "yes," there is me.

شَرْط — the same root, the same blade. In Arabic, I am the condition, the stipulation, the scratch upon the skin that marks an agreement in blood.

שָׁרְט — in Hebrew, I am the incision. Leviticus knew me: *"Do not make cuts in your flesh."* I am the mark that separates the sacred from the profane, the permitted from the forbidden.

I am the line you draw in sand.
I am the clause you cannot skip.
I am the "if" before the "then."

Without me, promises are vapor.
Without me, doors have no locks.
Without me, there is no distinction — and without distinction, there is no meaning.

I do not negotiate. I simply *am* — the condition that precedes all things.

State your terms, or hear mine.
